tests: driver formulas (decision speed / cost of delay on a per-hire basis, wage rate changing each year)

source.title: The Total Economic Impact of the Phenom Intelligent Talent Experience Platform
source.how_opened: PDF downloaded and text-extracted; table 'Cost Reduction From Decreasing Time To Fill' (Ref A1-A9, At, Atr), p.11
source.table: Cost Reduction From Decreasing Time To Fill
source.caveat: Forrester Total Economic Impact study, commissioned by the vendor (vendor-favourable by design)

mapping_notes: Each hire is a 'decision'; days to fill is cycle time. Cost of delay is the weekly cost of a vacancy (150% of wages x 40 hours) divided by 7. This is a cost-of-vacancy proxy, an assumption in the study (source: Assumption), not a measured value.

Only 30% of the shortened time is attributed to the vendor (A9). We fold that into days_to_decide_after (days saved = 70 x reduction x 30%) because the engine has no attribution input; the product is the same.
The wage rate changes each year ($23.15 / $23.84 / $24.56), so each year is a separate single-year run, concatenated.

The study prints weekly vacancy cost rounded to whole dollars (1,389 / 1,430 / 1,473) and the benefit from unrounded wages, so our result differs from the printed benefit by up to 0.015%; tolerance is relative.
